data.content_ref: inline:SRC_03 argues against the panel using a 'dense adversarial edge cases' task space and an infinite-dimensional expert intuition vs. a finite checklist, but it never addresses the half of the problem that asks for evidence within a single evaluation distinguishing genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance. Its mechanism only establishes that a finite checklist can be incomplete; it offers no single-evaluation evidence criterion, nor any way to tell whether the panel's advantage (if any) reflects genuine reliability rather than compliance that happens to track the right answer. Thus it answers only the for/against side and ignores the distinguishing-evidence requirement.
